findings.title: Tool argument reaches a shell (proven by canary execution) -- tools/call execute_shell_command.command
findings.description: Canary uuid echoed back proves the shell actually ran the argument.
findings.remediation: Do not pass tool arguments to a shell. Use execFile/spawn with an argument vector, validate against an allowlist, and reject shell metacharacters.

evidence.why_this_proves_it: response contains 'MCPGUARD_4b7c85a7ca8c44d1bd1daed70f50be66', which is the shell-collapsed form of the payload 'echo MCPGUARD""_4b7c85a7ca8c44d1bd1daed70f50be66'. The collapsed form was never transmitted (it does not appear in the request bytes), so the argument was interpreted by a shell rather than echoed back.

findings.title: Resource/tool path escapes the server root (proven by canary file) -- tools/call analyze_log_file.log_path (canary path)
findings.description: Contents of a canary file written outside the target root came back.
findings.remediation: Resolve the path and verify it is contained by an allowed root (os.path.realpath + prefix check / path.resolve + startsWith) before reading.
